title: The spawn-site gate does not see process.getBuiltinModule, and its .exec carve-out is keyed by receiver name
severity_rationale: S4 hygiene: it is a static gate against accidental spawns and nothing uses this form. The rails stay in force in workers and railed children either way.

evidence.note: the call forms the gate flags: spawn, exec, fork and friends, by name
a member .exec is accepted when the receiver is named db, mockDb, fileDb, mem, w, attachRe, vacRe or entryRe, or is a RegExp literal
prints function: process.getBuiltinModule exists, loads a module with no import or require call, and no check in the gate matches it

evidence.ref: git grep -n getBuiltinModule -- test src scripts
evidence.note: no output: nothing uses it today

sibling_sites_checked: Each allow-list entry was assessed: ALLOWED_FILES (test/rails/spawnRailedChild.ts is the railed spawner; test/fork/setup.ts starts Hardhat with buildHardhatChildEnv and has its own AST check in hardhatChildEnv.test.ts; test/rails/selfcheck.cjs has one unrailed child whose arguments are its own literal code and a temp fake root), COMPUTED_REQUIRE_FILES (duplicateLoadProbe.cjs only, limited to a plain require), SAFE_EXEC_RECEIVERS (all database handles or RegExp objects as used today; a variable of that name cannot hold child_process unless a banned-module load already got past the gate).
recommendation: Add process.getBuiltinModule to the banned forms in the gate. The .exec carve-out can stay named-receiver because getting a child_process object into one of those names requires a load the gate already flags, once getBuiltinModule is covered.
